title: The Most Useful School in the World Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. No murder occurs -- the 'crime' is Oki Shinobu staging a fake theft (smashing the vase herself and hiding the shards) to halt a live TV appraisal that would have publicly exposed her master Kimijima's prized vase as a counterfeit; `label.murderer_id` is kept as the schema field name but points to the staged-theft culprit. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep636-637...) already had the correct culprit (Oki Shinobu, s8) and correctly captured the deathbed-promise motive in its e1/e2 events, so no reversal was needed there -- but it was drastically underpopulated: it had zero relationship edges, one flat object node, no was_at coverage for most of the 11 suspects, and omitted several named characters who matter to the plot (Okino Yoko, whose hammer strike unwittingly masked the sound of the smash; Kimijima's late wife, who is the actual source of the secrecy motive; Takikawa the college professor, who supplies the red-herring 'disappearing object' theory that gets explicitly ruled out on-screen; and Yamazaki's unrelated handkerchief/photo subplot with Yoko, which is the episode's genuine red herring). case_type: staged_theft/concealment (no homicide).

clues.desc: No container leaving the studio was ever big enough to hold the vase whole, yet a whole vase went missing -- meaning it left in shard-sized pieces inside a small waist pouch, not carried out intact.
Honma called the vase 'Remarkable' both times he examined it -- first read as awe at a masterpiece, actually recognition of a masterful counterfeit.
